purpose: Matched regulator-authored product examples for testing whether pharmacological species/model relevance is associated with retention versus omission/tailoring of conventional animal toxicology. This is a hypothesis-generating comparator set, not a causal dataset.
outcome_definition: Primary outcome emphasizes general/repeat-dose toxicology. Endpoint-specific omissions are coded separately and routine ICH exclusions are not treated as species-relevance displacement unless the regulator explicitly links omission to model/species relevance.

comparators.modality: TCR bispecific / immune-mobilizing monoclonal TCR against cancer
comparators.jurisdiction: United States / European Union / Australia / Canada
comparators.species_relevance_basis: Regulators describe tebentafusp as human-specific with no pharmacologically relevant animal species for conventional nonclinical toxicology.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: No pharmacologically relevant conventional toxicology species; selected nonclinical work did not provide a conventional relevant-species toxicology program.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: EMA found no relevant animal model for formal safety evaluation; PMDA independently found no pharmacologically relevant rodent or NHP species because of BCMA cross-reactivity limitations.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: Selected mouse xenograft/non-GLP work for narrower pharmacology or off-target questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: The patient-specific genetically modified human T-cell product was considered inappropriate for administration to immunocompetent animals as a standard toxicity strategy.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: Immunocompromised-mouse studies for selected persistence/tumour-growth questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Health Canada records that no in vitro, ex vivo or in vivo model could accurately examine the toxicological characteristics of the individualized human product.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: Surrogate animal pharmacology for selected questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Product-specific human-cell therapy risk assessment and absence of a representative conventional toxicity strategy; EMA materials further identify lack of species cross-reactivity.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: Selected nonclinical work for narrower product-specific questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: The autologous single-infusion cell product did not support a conventional repeated-dose toxicity strategy; appropriate animal toxicity models were limited.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: NSG mouse xenograft pharmacology for tumour-control questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Health Canada records that no representative in vitro, ex vivo or in vivo model could accurately address toxicological characteristics of the engineered human T-cell product.
comparators.animal_studies_retained: Murine anti-CD19 surrogate pharmacology for selected questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Off-target and cross-reactivity questions for the engineered human TCR were addressed in human-relevant systems rather than through a conventional general-toxicology battery.
Health Canada states that nonclinical evaluation was limited by species specificity; appropriate models were absent for embryofetal development assessment.
endpoint_specific_omissions: embryofetal development due to absence of appropriate animal model
human_relevant_evidence: EMA materials describe human-tissue in vitro target-organ assessment
comparators.animal_studies_retained: A GLP main toxicity study was conducted.

comparators.modality: DLL3 x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager
comparators.species_relevance_basis: Monkey CD3 and DLL3 are sufficiently similar for tarlatamab binding; cynomolgus monkeys were selected for toxicological analysis, although relevance of normal-tissue DLL3 biology to cancer patients was qualified.
human_relevant_evidence: multiple model systems and clinical risk mitigation
comparators.animal_studies_retained: 10-day, one-month and three-month repeat-dose cynomolgus toxicology; mouse surrogate and xenograft studies for selected questions.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Cynomolgus monkey was the sole pharmacologically relevant species.
endpoint_specific_omissions: carcinogenicity/mutagenicity/genotoxicity not conducted under biologic conventions; not coded as species-relevance displacement
comparators.animal_studies_retained: General toxicity up to 39 weeks in cynomolgus monkeys plus pregnancy/developmental assessment in monkeys.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Health Canada explicitly describes cynomolgus monkey as a pharmacologically relevant species for pivotal toxicology.
endpoint_specific_omissions: carcinogenicity/genotoxicity not conducted under relevant ICH guidance; not coded as species-relevance displacement
comparators.animal_studies_retained: 13-week and 26-week repeat-dose toxicology plus male/female fertility-related and enhanced pre/postnatal development studies in cynomolgus monkeys.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Cemiplimab does not bind rodent PD-1; cynomolgus monkey was the only pharmacologically relevant species, supported by similar human/monkey tissue cross-reactivity.
human_relevant_evidence: ex vivo human and cynomolgus tissue cross-reactivity
comparators.animal_studies_retained: Three repeat-dose cynomolgus monkey toxicology studies for up to 26 weeks, including immunotoxicology, fertility and safety-pharmacology parameters.

comparators.species_relevance_basis: Crovalimab bound human and cynomolgus monkey C5 and reduced hemolysis in both sera, supporting cynomolgus monkey as the only pharmacologically relevant species.
endpoint_specific_omissions: genotoxicity/carcinogenicity not warranted under relevant guidelines; not coded as species-relevance displacement
human_relevant_evidence: in vitro human and cynomolgus serum hemolysis assays
comparators.animal_studies_retained: 5-week and 6-month repeat-dose cynomolgus toxicology plus enhanced prenatal/postnatal development study.
